_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Written from scratch for Raptor.
name: Minecraft: Geyser
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Geyser on its own, a proxy that lets Minecraft: Bedrock Edition players join a Java server. Installs any Geyser version and build, checked against GeyserMC's checksums, and points it at the Java server you choose.
startup: set --; case "{{JAVA_ADDRESS}}" in 127.0.0.1 | localhost) read -r _ _ gw _ < <(ip -4 route show default); [ -z "$gw" ] || set -- "--java.address=$gw" ;; esac; read -r need 2>/dev/null < .raptor-java || need=17; java -version 2>&1 | awk -F'"' -v need="$need" '/version/ { split($2, v, "."); have = (v[1] == "1") ? v[2] : v[1]; if (have + 0 < need + 0) { printf "This Geyser version needs Java %s or newer, and the server runs Java %s. Choose Java %s in Startup, then start the server again.\n", need, have, need; exit 1 } exit }' && exec java -Xms128M -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=85.0 -XX:+IgnoreUnrecognizedVMOptions -XX:+UseG1GC -XX:+ParallelRefProcEnabled -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200 -Dterminal.jline=false -Dterminal.ansi=true -jar {{SERVER_JARFILE}} --nogui "$@"

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Minecraft: Geyser. Downloads the standalone Geyser build from GeyserMC
# and checks it against GeyserMC's checksum. Its settings, extensions and
# packs are never touched, and the jar is only replaced once the new one
# checks out.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server

api=https://download.geysermc.org/v2/projects/geyser
ua="raptor-egg-library/1.0 (+https://raptorpanel.net)"
jar="${SERVER_JARFILE:-Geyser.jar}"
get() { curl -fsSL --retry 3 -A "$ua" "$1"; }
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }

versions=$(get "$api") || fail "GeyserMC can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
version="${GEYSER_VERSION:-latest}"
build="${BUILD_NUMBER:-latest}"
if [ "$version" = latest ]; then
    version=$(jq -r '.versions[-1]' <<<"$versions")
else
    jq -e --arg v "$version" 'any(.versions[]; . == $v)' <<<"$versions" >/dev/null ||
        fail "Geyser has no version $version. Set Version to latest, or to one Geyser has, such as $(jq -r '.versions[-1]' <<<"$versions")."
fi
code=$(curl -sSL --retry 3 -A "$ua" -o /tmp/geyser-build.json -w '%{http_code}' "$api/versions/$version/builds/$build") ||
    fail "GeyserMC can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
[ "$code" = 404 ] && fail "Geyser $version has no build $build. Set Build to latest, or to one of its builds."
[ "$code" = 200 ] || fail "GeyserMC can't be reached right now (HTTP $code). Reinstall to try again."
id=$(jq -r .build /tmp/geyser-build.json)
sum=$(jq -r '.downloads.standalone.sha256 // empty' /tmp/geyser-build.json)
[ -n "$sum" ] || fail "Geyser $version build $id has no standalone jar. Choose another build."

if [ -f "$jar" ] && [ "$(sha256sum "$jar" | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$sum" ]; then
    echo "Geyser $version build $id is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading Geyser $version build $id"
    curl -fsSL --retry 3 -A "$ua" -o "$jar.new" "$api/versions/$version/builds/$id/downloads/standalone" ||
        { rm -f "$jar.new"; fail "The download from GeyserMC failed. Reinstall to try again."; }
    [ "$(sha256sum "$jar.new" | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$sum" ] ||
        { rm -f "$jar.new"; fail "The download didn't match GeyserMC's checksum. Reinstall to try again."; }
    mv -f "$jar.new" "$jar"
fi

# The Java the jar needs, from its main class (the manifest wraps long
# lines): the startup command checks it.
main=$(unzip -p "$jar" META-INF/MANIFEST.MF | tr -d '\r' | awk '/^Main-Class:/ { m = $2; c = 1; next } c && /^ / { m = m substr($0, 2); next } { c = 0 } END { print m }')
major=$(unzip -p "$jar" "${main//.//}.class" 2>/dev/null | od -An -j6 -N2 -tu1 | awk 'NF == 2 { print $1 * 256 + $2 - 44 }') || true
java="${major:-17}"
echo "$java" > .raptor-java

# Geyser fills in the rest of its settings on its first start; the Panel
# sets the ports and the Java server in it.
[ -s config.yml ] || printf 'bedrock:\n  address: 0.0.0.0\n  port: %s\njava:\n  address: 127.0.0.1\n  port: 25565\nenable-metrics: false\n' "${SERVER_PORT:-19132}" > config.yml
echo "Installed Geyser $version build $id. It needs Java $java or newer."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Geyser version, such as 2.12.1, or latest for the newest one. Reinstall the server after changing it.

variables.name: Build
variables.description: The Geyser build for that version, or latest for its newest build.

variables.name: Jar file
variables.description: The name of Geyser's jar file.

variables.name: Java server address
variables.description: The address of the Java server Bedrock players join, such as play.example.com; 127.0.0.1 means a server on this same machine.

variables.name: Java server port
variables.description: The port of that Java server.

variables.name: Sign-in
variables.description: How Bedrock players sign in to the Java server: online (each needs a Java account), offline (the Java server is in offline mode), or floodgate (no Java account, with the Floodgate plugin on the Java server).

variables.name: Usage statistics
variables.description: Send anonymous statistics about the server to bStats.org, where its developers see them (true or false).
